text:
Muscle lactate production rises when glycolysis produces pyruvate faster than the mitochondria can oxidize it, which happens during high-intensity exercise with heavy fast-twitch fiber recruitment. Hypoxia, a high cytosolic NADH/NAD⁺ ratio, and epinephrine stimulation also push glycolysis, and therefore lactate, higher. Lactate output falls when exercise intensity drops to a level the oxidative system can match.

CONFIDENCE: 90
